doc.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Clarinet, home jam sessions and teacher Chief McNally
summary: His high school teacher Chief McNally, a former road trombonist, and his father taking him to Condon's in New York.

bands.name: Red Nichols and His Five Pennies

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: in this sax section just, just loving it. And so then I got a clarinet because you know you have to double, and so I thought of myself as a clarinetist and saxophone player. My dad at this point began having jam sessions in our house and we’d invite people over. And my high school music teacher, a guy named Chief McNally, who was a trombonist, had been brought up and his parents were Salvation Army folks. And you’re not supposed to leave the Army. You’re supposed to stay in the Salvation Army if you’re a child. But he was so good he went on the road with some big bands, played with Red Nichols and then got in the Navy and came home, fell in love with one of his childhood sweethearts who was also a Salvation Army child and she convinced him — she couldn’t convince him to go back into the Salvation Army but she did convince him to come off the road and to be a music teacher. So he was my teacher. This is a long story.
It was a bit of a compromise on his part but a good one.
